newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm, tracking swaps and crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm, tracking swaps and crude gains.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market firmed in line with stronger swaps quotes and crude gains, traders said on Friday.
Sentiment was also firmer ahead of the maintenance turnarounds of two refineries in Singapore, traders said.
Mobil 280,000-bpd refinery will be shutdown for six weeks starting March 15 and Singapore Refining Co's refinery will shut an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker unit from March 2-22.
In the swaps market, February paper was last quoted at $102.00/$103.00, up from $99.00/$100.50 a day-earlier.
Traders said cash prices have tracked swaps quotes with bids for March barrels rising to $100.00 per tonne, up from Thursday's $99.00 per tonne.
Offers have disappeared as previously unsold supplies appeared to have been absorbed, traders said.
"Chinese demand is also emerging," said one trader.
Thailand has yet to award its tender to buy 10,000 tones of 1.0 percent sulphur grade fuel oil for delivery March 3-7 on Friday.

Taiwan purchased tender has aslo helped boost levels. Taiwan has bought three cargoes of low pour 0.5-percent sulphur grade fuel oil instead of the one it had originally tendered for. The three 38,000 tonnes cargo were purchased at $142.50 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
